params.requirement: Turns a briefed request into a draft manifest: strict JSON in a closed vocabulary, following long instructions and tool results exactly. It needs precise instruction following and reliable structured output of up to many thousands of tokens, after a medium deliberation (GH #1300). An operator waits on it, so an answer within a few minutes is required, the price per call should stay moderate, and a model served locally is welcome.

api_key.description: Provider API key. Deprecated, removed in 0.63.0: name a grant in credential_grant_id instead (#801).

credential_grant_id.description: GH #801: the grant this cell presents to get its provider credential SEALED from an access hive instead of carrying a key. It ships EMPTY, which is no grant at all; whoever grows the cell (the builder recipe or the colony's own template) sets it through `override_params`, and the credential then arrives over the credential v-lane and is opened in RAM only. Immutable: a new grant is a new instance.

external_timeout_ms_row.description: GH #1097: not read by the cell -- the catalogue row its `external_timeout_ms` and `cell.message_timeout` are derived from (the timeout chain, docs/cell-types.md § llm): the row of the model this cell is born on. A manifest that bears it on another row derives both again from that row.

reasoning_effort.description: GH #1300: how long the model deliberates before it answers, in the provider's shorthand (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `none` = off, or the lowest effort a model that cannot switch thinking off takes; passed through, not checked against a list). It ships `medium`, the effort every shipped llm cell runs at unless its instance says otherwise: an instance sets it through `override_params` on this cell's path, and a registry push that names no effort resets it to this birth value. On the chat-completions wire it goes out as `"reasoning": {"effort": ...}` (default `reasoning_wire`), on the Anthropic Messages wire as `output_config.effort`; `none` switches thinking off in the form the model takes. A `reasoning` object, where one is set, outranks it; a model whose catalogue `supported_params` omits the field never receives it.

description.purpose: The one model call of the design lane: it turns a briefed request into a draft manifest. `provider` names the WIRE PROTOCOL, not the vendor, so any OpenAI-shaped endpoint serves -- including the stub the scenario suite starts, which is why the composed class is provable at zero cost. The system tree has a third slot since GH #485: `budget`, rendered fresh by the fan-in on every re-briefing rather than parked with the instructions -- it says which round this is, how many are left, and that the last one is offered no tools at all. It is deliberately NOT in `system_order`: `concat_system_prompt` appends the slots that are not named there after the ones that are, so the budget lands LAST in the prompt -- which is where a rule about THIS round belongs -- and the declared order stays the two slots every other shipped llm cell declares.
description.not_in_scope: No parsing and no trust: whatever it answers is read by `normalise` before it becomes a manifest. And no boot-time demand: all three variables carry an EMPTY default. This hive travels inside the OS shell, and a shell that could not be grown without a model credential would make the FAST LANE -- which asks no model at all -- conditional on one. A colony with no composer configured still rewires an edge; what it cannot do fails at call time, loudly, and not at boot. The completion budget is the model's catalogue `max_output` (`max_tokens` 0, GH #1097 / R-HK-13), and it is a CEILING rather than a spend: a completion is billed by what it produces, so the only thing the cap buys is room to answer in ONE turn -- and what this cell answers with is a whole manifest, up to `normalise`'s declaration cap, which for a rendered level is thousands of tokens of JSON. A cap that is too small does not save the call, it truncates it: `finish_reason: length` on a half-written JSON object is read by `normalise` as `no_manifest_in_answer`, which is a round paid for and nothing delivered. The one thing that DID make a large ceiling expensive was deliberation, because a reasoning model spends the ceiling first and bills all of it -- measured on a design build's writing round: the entire budget spent on reasoning, `finish_reason: length`, content empty, 0.39 USD. Since GH #1097 the ceiling is the catalogue's `max_output`, so a medium deliberation (below) spends its tokens under a ceiling it cannot exhaust. Deliberation runs at `medium` since GH #1300 (owner ruling: every shipped llm cell, every Anthropic model, effort medium), declared as `reasoning_effort`. From GH #498 until then `reasoning` was declared OFF, because an unsent field handed the decision to the provider's default -- measured against a hosted Sonnet-class model on a design build's writing round, that default returned 967 completion tokens of which 965 were reasoning and a content of "" under the old small cap; on the Anthropic wire the OFF object was not a form the Messages API reads, and the cell ran at the model's own default (high on Sonnet 5.5). A build that wants another depth sets it where every other tuning decision in this hive is made -- `override_params` addressing this cell and `reasoning_effort` (`none` switches it off in the form the model takes).
